title: Real-time cellular and molecular vision of the intact operative field

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a surgical imaging system that continuously identifies cells, tissue types or molecular targets across the intact working field, including tissue at the plane being dissected. The surgeon would receive a spatial display broad and fast enough to guide an operation without removing a specimen for each reading. Its scope would be defined by the tissues and targets it can identify, the area and depth it covers, and how reliably it updates during surgery. This is a proposed capability, not an achievement established by the supplied evidence.

The motivating gap is the distance between obtaining microscopic information at selected locations and maintaining useful microscopic guidance across a changing surgical field. The supplied confocal literature documents small imaging fields, limited penetration and interference from movement and blood. The brain-tumor study also describes wide-field 5-ALA fluorescence as providing less cellular architectural detail than confocal imaging. These examples explain the goal without establishing that all existing imaging fits one classification or that every fluorescence technique has the same limitations.

Conceptual distinction: resolving cell-sized structures is only one component. A useful display must also establish what those structures are, or which molecular targets are present, with validated specificity. Cellular appearance, molecular identity, tissue perfusion and preserved physiological function are different measurements. The proposed system need not measure all of them, but its display must make clear which information it actually provides.

significance.text: If achieved, this capability would extend microscopic assessment from selected spots to the field that guides dissection. This matters particularly where tumor and normal tissue intermingle: the supplied brain-tumor study identifies infiltrating glioma margins as difficult to discriminate and interpret. Continuous, validated identification could reduce dependence on choosing the right biopsy location and could map detectable residual disease while the operation remains open. Those are conditional consequences of the proposed capability; fewer sampling errors and better diagnostic decisions would still require clinical demonstration.

Conditional impact synthesis: validated identification of nerves, vessels and tissue boundaries could help surgeons select a dissection plane and avoid critical structures. The benefit would depend on performance in the particular tissue, including whether the relevant boundary lies within imaging depth and remains visible during manipulation. Recognizing a nerve does not establish that it still conducts, and recognizing a vessel does not establish adequate blood flow. Safer dissection, improved function and better patient outcomes would therefore be additional findings to demonstrate.

Better visualization would not itself remove every infiltrating malignant cell or prevent recurrence. The brain-tumor study discusses the difficulty of complete clearance in highly infiltrative disease and calls for further evaluation of resection and survival outcomes. Disease below detection limits, beyond imaging depth or outside the operative field would remain important boundaries. Complete selective removal while preserving an organ, and control of disease elsewhere in the body, require capabilities beyond this imaging advance.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved integration is obtaining useful coverage, depth, specificity and speed together under operative conditions. The supplied gastrointestinal confocal review documents microscopic fields and superficial penetration, including the inability to see deeper structures in the described applications. The brain-tumor study reports that scanning speed limited rapid inspection of large areas. Improving image quality at one contact point would address only part of the proposed field-scale capability.

Blood and motion are demonstrated engineering obstacles. In the brain-tumor study, more than half of acquired images were uninterpretable, commonly because of motion distortion or obscuration by clumped red blood cells. A system intended to guide ongoing dissection would need to maintain useful coverage through these disturbances, or promptly indicate where information is unavailable. High diagnostic accuracy on selected interpretable images cannot by itself establish that the working field is reliably visible.

Engineering synthesis: the display must also remain aligned with tissue as the surgeon moves, deforms or removes it. Identification must distinguish the intended targets from nearby normal tissue, including ambiguous transition zones, and must communicate uncertainty without creating false confidence. Combining microscopy, molecular probes and image interpretation may contribute, but the supplied evidence does not establish a particular architecture that solves these requirements. Image acquisition, interpretation and display must together fit the pace of the intended operation.

current_state.text: A gastrointestinal probe-based confocal laser endomicroscopy review published on November 3, 2025 reports approximately 1 µm lateral resolution and an imaging depth of approximately 55–70 µm for the systems summarized. It describes pCLE as an adjunct rather than a routine standard and identifies superficial penetration, narrow fields, operator dependence and interpretation variability as limitations. Its body also discusses superficial imaging up to approximately 250 µm, so 55–70 µm should not be treated as a universal depth limit for all confocal systems. These findings concern gastrointestinal applications rather than an exhaustive survey of surgical imaging. The supplied review assessed retained article text; figures were not visually inspected.

A single-institution brain-tumor feasibility study published on May 14, 2025 enrolled 50 patients during 2020–2023 and evaluated intraoperative in vivo confocal imaging with a handheld system. Real-time neuropathology consultation occurred in 27 cases. The reported mean of 10.5 seconds measures time from the start of scanning to the first interpretable image, not time to a completed diagnostic consultation. The study demonstrates acquisition of cellular tissue images at selected operative locations; it does not demonstrate continuous identification across the whole field during dissection.

The same study's abstract and results prose report 93% sensitivity and 81% specificity against permanent histology, whereas Table 3 reports 92% sensitivity, with a reported interval of 83–96%, and 80% specificity, with an interval of 61–91%, for all CLE specimens. The supplied review found no explanation reconciling these overall estimates. Glioma-margin specificity was 50%, compared with 93% in the core, underscoring that performance at the clinically difficult boundary can differ substantially from performance within a lesion. The article also contains discrepancies between abstract and body counts of images and regions of interest, leaving exact denominators unresolved.

More than half of acquired images in that study were uninterpretable, most commonly because of motion or clumped red blood cells. This statement concerns individual images; it does not mean that more than half of patients or sampled regions yielded no usable image. Regions with non-interpretable imaging were excluded from the diagnostic analysis. The retained full discussion supports these findings directly, superseding the earlier research's reliance on a search excerpt. Image yield and diagnostic accuracy therefore describe different aspects of performance and must be considered together.

The earlier research identifies a stimulated Raman histology study attributed to Nohman and colleagues, reportedly published online on November 17, 2024. It describes label-free production of hematoxylin-and-eosin-like specimen images in minutes, a 70-case brain-tumor cohort, an AUC of 0.77 for diagnostic agreement and a workflow testing one specimen at a time. These remain reported claims rather than verified findings in this record: the only retained PubMed extraction contained a cookie notice, so the supplied evidence review could not confirm the article's identity or scientific content. That extraction failure does not establish that the reported findings are false.

Evidence boundary: the supplied materials establish dated confocal demonstrations and their limitations, but contain no usable freshness-search results establishing the state of the entire field as of November 1, 2026. They therefore support the proposed research goal without proving that no other modality or subsequent development meets some or all of its scope.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: during an open or minimally invasive human operation, an integrated system should display validated cellular or molecular identities across a continuous field large enough to guide the intended dissection, including tissue at the cutting plane, without requiring specimen removal for every reading. The protocol should specify field dimensions, depth, update rate, end-to-end latency and how coverage is maintained as the field changes. Isolated contact-probe readings or a virtual stain of an excised specimen would not alone demonstrate this scope. These are proposed criteria, not established regulatory thresholds.
completion_criteria.label: Validated cellular or molecular identities span the operative cutting plane

completion_criteria.text: Proposed validation: a prespecified human series should compare the display with location-matched histology for the tissues relevant to the intended operations, including nerve, vessel, tumor and normal parenchyma where applicable. Tissue-specific performance targets should be set before evaluation, with particular attention to margins and mixed tissue. The study should report unavailable and uninterpretable regions alongside diagnostic results, rather than judging the system only where it produces a usable image. Location-matched histology and the exclusion of uninterpretable regions in the supplied confocal study provide practical motivation for this design.
completion_criteria.label: Location-matched human histology comparisons report tissue-specific performance and unusable regions

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and boundaries: independent teams should reproduce performance across the intended operators, procedures and operative conditions, including blood, motion and tissue deformation. Reports should identify which targets, tissue states, depths and field sizes were tested, how long useful coverage persisted, and where performance failed. A finite series establishes demonstrated breadth within those conditions, not universal tissue recognition. Claims of fewer errors, improved resection, preserved function or better outcomes should require additional clinical comparisons appropriate to each claimed benefit.
completion_criteria.label: Independent teams reproduce operative performance and report boundaries and failures

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: SUR-10, “Cell-identity-selective extirpation inside an organ that keeps working,” has the closest relationship. SUR-11 concerns seeing and identifying targets; SUR-10 concerns selectively removing them while maintaining organ function. Imaging could guide selective extirpation, but neither reliable removal nor preserved function follows from identification alone. The supplied roster title supports this distinction, although a detailed SUR-10 specification was not provided.

Roster-based synthesis: SUR-06, “Autonomous completion of whole operations at expert level,” could use continuous tissue identification as sensory input, but also requires operative decision-making and execution beyond imaging. SUR-07, “Incisionless resection and reconstruction inside the closed body,” concerns access and intervention; SUR-11 could potentially provide guidance in that setting, but does not itself supply incisionless access, resection or reconstruction.

Roster-based synthesis: SUR-01 and SUR-02 address transplant tolerance and xenotransplantation; SUR-03 addresses organ cryobanking; SUR-04 addresses restoration after complete spinal cord transection; SUR-05 addresses regenerative wound healing; SUR-08 addresses reversible metabolic arrest after traumatic exsanguination cardiac arrest; SUR-09 and SUR-12 address living replacements for complex parts and assembled autologous solid organs. Surgical imaging might assist procedures involving these advances, but their defining breakthroughs concern immunity, preservation, repair, physiological rescue or tissue construction. They remain distinct from continuous identification of the operative field, and their roster titles alone do not establish particular dependencies on SUR-11.

change_log.change: Preserved SUR-11's ID, title and field-scale imaging identity while defining validated targets, coverage, depth and operative timing.
change_log.reason: The concept remains coherent despite limitations in individual supporting assertions; clearer scope distinguishes it from isolated optical biopsies.

change_log.change: Replaced exhaustive claims about existing imaging and fluorescence with modality- and setting-specific limitations.
change_log.reason: The supplied evidence covers gastrointestinal pCLE and brain-tumor confocal imaging, not every imaging modality or all wide-field fluorescence.

change_log.change: Separated cellular resolution, tissue identity, molecular specificity, perfusion and physiological function.
change_log.reason: Visible cellular detail does not by itself establish molecular identity or preserved function.

change_log.change: Qualified the 55–70 µm depth range and retained the review's separate discussion of approximately 250 µm superficial imaging.
change_log.reason: The smaller range cannot be generalized to every confocal system.

change_log.change: Corrected the 10.5-second measure to time to the first interpretable image and added enrollment dates and consultation scope.
change_log.reason: Image acquisition time is different from completed diagnostic turnaround, and consultation occurred in only 27 of 50 cases.

change_log.change: Preserved both conflicting overall sensitivity/specificity estimates, the margin/core difference and unresolved image and region counts.
change_log.reason: The supplied review identifies internal discrepancies without evidence that resolves them.

change_log.change: Integrated full-text support for motion and blood artifacts and explained the exclusion of uninterpretable regions.
change_log.reason: The finding no longer depends solely on a search excerpt, and diagnostic accuracy must be interpreted alongside imaging availability.

change_log.change: Retained the Raman study's reported quantitative and workflow claims with explicit extraction limitations.
change_log.reason: A cookie-only retained artifact prevents confirmation but does not justify declaring the findings false or deleting the research lead.

change_log.change: Made clinical benefits conditional and expanded proposed completion criteria to include unavailable coverage, reproducibility and practical boundaries.
change_log.reason: Technical identification performance does not establish improved outcomes, and finite testing cannot prove universal recognition.

change_log.change: Used the supplied roster to distinguish SUR-10 and other related entries, and preserved the unresolved freshness boundary.
change_log.reason: The roster supplies useful conceptual titles absent from the earlier review, while no supplied search establishes comprehensive field status through November 1, 2026.

unresolved_issues: Whether another modality or development through November 1, 2026 meets the full proposed scope remains unresolved because no usable freshness-search results were supplied.
The brain-tumor study's 93%/81% prose estimates and 92%/80% Table 3 estimates remain unreconciled, as do discrepancies in image and region counts.
The Raman study's identity, reported publication date, 70-case cohort, AUC of 0.77, processing time and single-specimen workflow could not be confirmed from the retained cookie-only extraction.
The intended operations, validated targets, field dimensions, depth, latency, performance targets and acceptable unavailable-imaging rates still require protocol-level definition.
Detailed specifications for the other roster entries were not supplied; related-concept comparisons are limited to their titles.

All substantive review recommendations were adopted. The review's inability to verify SUR-10's identity was partly addressed by the subsequently supplied roster title, while its detailed scope remains unverified.
